transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, it's so nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, I guess... well, I hope I'm in the right place, I really don't want to waste your time. But I've been having a little bit of trouble at work—I'm an auditor—and I usually try so hard to be on top of everything. I really do. But what finally pushed me to make this appointment is that... I keep starting my follow-up items after audits, or after these mentorship events we do, and I always have every intention of finishing them right then. But then, I don't know, I'll find out days later that the final email, or a review note, or some form just... never actually got done. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, honestly, because I really do care about my job and I don't want people to think I'm slacking off. Um, does that make sense? Is that something you might be able to help me with?
Before age 12, did you often have trouble finishing schoolwork or keeping track of assignments?

Oh, um... yes, actually. It's kind of funny you ask that, because my mother still jokes about it. She always says I was the kind of kid who could completely ace a test, but then I'd just... forget to turn in the big project that was sitting right there in my backpack. 

I really tried to be a good student, though! My teachers always wrote on my elementary school report cards that I was very bright, which was nice of them. But, um... I guess they did also say that I tended to lose assignments, or that I rushed past the small details. And I guess I maybe talked out of turn sometimes. I think I just got a little too eager to participate? But they did note that I needed reminders to finish my work. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like I was a bad kid... I really did want to do well and please my teachers. Is that... does that answer what you were asking?
Do you have this same kind of trouble staying organized or finishing tasks at home, too?

Oh... um, well... yes, I suppose I do. I try really hard to keep everything running smoothly at home, I promise I do. But... well, my husband is just so wonderful and patient, and he's actually had to step in and take over the bills and a lot of the social commitments I said I would handle. I always, always mean to do them! But I think it just got to the point where he felt he couldn't completely rely on me to finish them on time. It makes me feel terrible, honestly. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad partner... 

And, um... to be completely honest with you... I know I mentioned work earlier, but I might have held back a little bit. I was just so embarrassed. But those unfinished follow-ups... it actually reached the point recently where a client review was affected by my mistakes. I'm really worried that people at the firm are starting to question whether I can handle the promotion I've been working so hard for. I just want to be dependable for them, you know? 

I'm sorry, I know that's a lot. Does that... is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Do you get unwanted thoughts that keep coming back and are hard to stop?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, I definitely have a lot on my mind all the time, trying to keep track of work and home and everything. But I wouldn't say I have unwanted thoughts that get stuck or anything like that. 

I really try to keep a positive mindset, you know? I don't want to dwell on negative things or let my mind go to dark places. I just get a little... scattered, I guess, with the things I'm supposed to be doing. But not bad thoughts that I can't stop. 

I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I'm glad I don't have that, but I want to make sure I'm answering your question correctly. Is that what you meant?
Do you worry excessively about a lot of different things?

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say I do. I mean, of course I care very much about doing a good job for my clients, and I fret a little when I let my husband down... but I don't sit around worrying about all sorts of different things. I really try to be an optimistic person! I always want to look on the bright side and just keep trying my best to fix my mistakes. 

I hope that's okay? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm a constantly anxious person on top of being so disorganized. I try really hard to keep a smile on. Does... does that answer your question?
Did these attention and follow-through problems begin only after a medical illness or injury?

Oh, goodness, no. Um... I haven't had any major illnesses or injuries or anything like that. I've always been very healthy, thankfully! I try to take good care of myself. 

These issues... well, I feel like I've always had to work extra hard just to keep all my ducks in a row. It's just... maybe it's gotten a little harder to hide lately with all the responsibilities at the firm and at home. But it's definitely not from being sick or getting hurt. 

I hope that's helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information so we can figure this out.
